title: Claude Code Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits, and Costs
summary: Claude Code pricing breaks down into three tiers with different feature access and costs.
body_markdown:
## Claude Code spending control routine


Pick a monthly dollar ceiling, read your usage screen every Monday, and let a trigger you wrote in advance decide when to change plans. That way the worst week from that comparison gets priced before it happens.


It takes a few minutes once it's a habit, and it comes to six steps:


1. Set a monthly dollar budget.
2. Open the usage screen.
3. Note your session use and your weekly use.
4. Compare both with last week.
5. Apply the upgrade or downgrade trigger.
6. Record the decision.


### Set the budget and the trigger


Choose the budget as a number before looking at any dashboard, because a ceiling set after the fact will always sit just above whatever you spent.


Write down the plan that fits under it, then write the trigger: "I upgrade if I hit the weekly limit twice in a month. I downgrade if I finish a month well short of the session limit."


> Choose the budget as a number before looking at any dashboard, because a ceiling set after the fact will always sit just above whatever you spent.


Two hits means a pattern rather than one bad deadline, and the bill for upgrading is then a decision, not a reaction.


### Check usage weekly


Open the usage screen on the same day each week. Note two readings: how close your sessions got to their limit, and how much of the weekly allowance you consumed. The two are different failures.


Running into the session limit mid-task interrupts you but resets quickly, so it costs you time. Running into the weekly limit stops you for longer, so it costs you days.


On its own, a single reading tells you little, and the week-over-week change tells you whether your workload is growing into a bigger plan or shrinking out of the one you have.


Then apply the trigger exactly as written, and record what you did and why in a line or two. When the same question comes up in three months, you'll have your own history to settle it, not a vendor's marketing page.


### Automate the weekly spend summary with Activepieces


This step is for people billed through the API, where spend accrues per token and no plan limit stops you. Build a scheduled workflow in Activepieces that pulls your usage once a week and posts a short summary to wherever you already read messages.


A run costs 1 credit however many steps the workflow has, so adding a step to format or route the summary doesn't change the bill.


Think of it as housekeeping, not a replacement for the Monday check: it saves you collecting the numbers, while the decision stays yours.


At one run a week, that's four or five credits a month against the 1,000 included on[the free plan](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , which also allows unlimited flows, so this workflow doesn't need a paid tier.
